summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book (Book 3, part 18), the narrator Morgan visits fertility doctor Hannah Klein on the Upper West Side after a final failed intrauterine insemination attempt with husband Steve's sperm deposit. The pregnancy test confirms she is not pregnant, and Hannah suggests considering adoption. Morgan reflects that she feels liberated to stop the baby pursuit and must accept that the baby part of her life is over and move on to Plan B. The passage opens with reflections on Carly Grove, who found Kevin quickly, and on David's office, where the narrator had lunch of hot dogs.
one_line: Morgan receives confirmation that her final fertility attempt has failed and hears adoption suggested by Dr. Hannah Klein.
key_facts: Morgan's final attempt at pregnancy, another intrauterine insemination (IUI) using the last of Steve's sperm deposit, had failed.
Lori, the assistant of Hannah Klein, ran the pregnancy test that confirmed Morgan was not pregnant.
Hannah Klein's office is on the Upper West Side, and she has been a fixture there for about fifty years.
Hannah Klein was pushing seventy, was a chain smoker, and was a child of the Holocaust.
Hannah Klein told Morgan, "maybe you ought to just start considering adoption—if having a child still means that much to you."
Morgan describes IUI as med-speak for an expensive "turkey baster."
Morgan had no cysts, fibroids, polyps or ovulatory abnormalities, and her uterus and Fallopian tubes were fine.
Steve's sperm counts were okay, but no pregnancy occurred.
Morgan felt strangely liberated in Hannah Klein's office because she would never again have to endure the humiliation of those appointments.
Morgan ate two hot dogs with sauerkraut from a striped-umbrella vendor before going to Hannah Klein's office.
Morgan describes herself as a theoretically functional reproductive machine that just wouldn't kick over.
Carly Grove found Kevin in no time at all, with zero hassles, which the narrator finds mysterious.
Morgan hailed a cab clutching the grungy brown bag after leaving David's office.
Hannah Klein never wore perfume but always smelled faintly of roses mixed with something else.
